question.text: What national wholesale price for graded, loose, white Large shell eggs will the USDA AMS Egg Markets Overview dated November 13, 2026 report? (cents per dozen)
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the single price stated in the USDA AMS "Egg Markets Overview" report dated November 13, 2026, in the sentence reporting the "wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs" (the sentence typically reads like "Wholesale prices for national trading of truck lot quantities of graded, loose, white Large shell eggs were $0.01 lower at $0.28 per dozen with a steady undertone"). The edition is available from the AMS report archive at https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/3725 (select the 2026 releases and open the November 13, 2026 PDF) and, on its publication day, at https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/ams_3725.pdf. The value is expressed in cents per dozen: a report stating "$0.35 per dozen" resolves as 35, and a report stating "35 cents per dozen" also resolves as 35. Only that one price counts; other prices in the same report (New York formula cartoned, Midwest warehouse-delivered, Midwest producer, California benchmarks, breaking stock, egg products) are disregarded.
question.fine_print: If the edition dated November 13, 2026 is not published, or is published without this line, this question resolves to the value for the same line in the next edition of the Egg Markets Overview that reports it. If the report stops publishing this line entirely and no later edition reports it, the question is annulled.

research:
I found no November 6 or November 13 edition yet. The latest daily data suggests the market is firming, though. The weekly report's line appears to be the Friday value of the USDA's daily 5-day rolling index, rounded: the October 30 edition said $0.35 and the October 30 daily index was 34.90¢. My figures are all from secondary sites (IndexBox, The Scramble) that republish USDA data, not from the USDA files themselves.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-04: The live AMS PDF (ams_3725.pdf) loads (status 200), but my tool can't read PDF text, so I couldn't confirm which edition it currently holds. [AMS](https://www.ams.usda.gov/mnreports/ams_3725.pdf)
- 2026-10-30 edition (latest I could confirm): national loose white Large eggs up 7¢ to 35¢/dozen, steady undertone. Midwest warehouse-delivered steady at 54¢, Midwest producer price 36¢, California benchmark $1.10. [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-egg-markets-overview-wholesale-egg-prices-rise-as-inventories-climb/)
- The leading daily series is the USDA Daily National Shell Egg Index (AMS 2843), a 5-day weighted average for conventional graded loose white Large eggs. [AMS 2843](https://mymarketnews.ams.usda.gov/viewReport/2843)
  - 2026-11-02: 35.42¢ (prior 34.90), range 21-54¢, 25,728 cases. Undertone steady to firm, light demand for loose eggs. [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-daily-shell-egg-index-report-national-prices-steady-to-higher-on-2-november-2026/)
  - 2026-11-03: 39.36¢, up 3.94¢, 36,000 cases. Undertone steady to firm, moderate retail demand, light domestic demand for loose eggs, moderate to good export demand. Supplies moderate to fully adequate, Medium eggs tighter. 6-Area shell egg inventory up 3.9% on the week. A year earlier it was 175.32¢. [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-daily-national-shell-egg-index-report-nov-3-2026/)
  - Recent sequence per The Scramble: 33.1, then 34.5, 34.9 (Oct 30), 35.4 (Nov 2), 39.4 (Nov 3). That is up 26% week over week but down 14.7% from 46.1¢ a month earlier. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/national/large-white)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The November 6 edition had not been published as of this research. The daily index was 39.4¢ on 2026-11-03, already above the 35¢ weekly print and still rising. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/national/large-white)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: New York store-door Large white quoted at 79-83¢. The weekly report's New York formula price was 72¢ on Oct 30, but these may be on different bases, so I can't say for sure that New York firmed. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/national/large-white)
- 2026-11-03: Other sizes moved in different directions. Extra Large rose 38.9% on the week to 41.3¢. Medium was 23.0¢ as of Oct 30, down 18.6%. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/national/large-white)
- 2026-11-02: National shell egg inventory was 1,653 thousand 30-dozen cases, 15% above the 5-year median. Supply is heavy, which pushes against the price rise. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/)
- 2026-10-26 week: Midwest, Northeast, Southeast and South Central warehouse-delivered prices were all unchanged. [The Scramble](https://the-scramble.com/national/large-white)
- HPAI: The Scramble's weekly brief for the week of Oct 19 counted 14 detections and 17.0M layer birds year to date, including the 934,600-bird Illinois flock confirmed Oct 19. I found no confirmed US layer detections dated November 2026, and I couldn't verify the October 28 California detection mentioned in the question background. [The Scramble HPAI](https://the-scramble.com/hpai/layer-flocks)

## 4. Base rates
- The 2026 weekly series runs from about 24¢ (mid-June) to about 151¢ (March). Recent prints: Sep 4 35, Sep 18 35, Sep 25 39, Oct 2 about 46 (per IndexBox), Oct 9 43, Oct 16 29, Oct 23 28, Oct 30 35. Over the two weeks from Oct 9 to Oct 23 the price fell 15¢. Over the two weeks from Oct 16 to Oct 30 it rose 6¢. [IndexBox](https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-egg-markets-overview-wholesale-egg-prices-rise-as-inventories-climb/)
- Year-earlier comparison: the daily index was about 164-175¢ in early November 2025, and an October 2025 edition printed $1.16. Last year's levels were much higher and HPAI-driven, so they say little about this year's level. I couldn't find the November 14, 2025 edition to check the seasonal direction. [Poultry Times](https://www.poultrytimes.com/?p=17496)
- Because the daily index is a 5-day rolling average, a jump like Nov 3's reflects higher individual trades that will keep feeding the average through the week.

## 5. Other forecasts
- No prediction market covers this weekly line.
- Polymarket "Price of Dozen Eggs in October" (this is the BLS retail price, a different measure): $2.20-2.30 at 0.675.
- Kalshi "Egg prices up in October" (CPI): Yes at 0.33.
- Neither market matches this question; both are retail measures.
- I found no expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-06 (Fri): Egg Markets Overview edition, likely to roughly match the Nov 6 daily index.
- Daily AMS 2843 index every business day through Nov 13; the Nov 13 daily value is probably the best proxy for the answer.
- Weekly inventory and Shell Egg Demand Indicator updates.
- Any APHIS-confirmed layer detection, especially a large Midwest one.
- Pre-Thanksgiving retail feature buying.
- The NASS Chickens and Eggs report (about Nov 20) and the ERS Outlook (about Nov 17) both come after resolution.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days. The November 13, 2026 edition publishes Friday afternoon, around 22:00 UTC.

(b) The latest weekly print is 35¢/dozen (Oct 30, 2026, up 7¢). The daily 5-day index, which the weekly line appears to track, was 39.4¢ on Nov 3, up from 34.9¢ on Oct 30. These daily figures come from secondary sites, not the USDA files.

(c) If nothing changed, the outcome would be about 35-39¢.

(d) If the trend continued, the outcome would be about 45-55¢. The index rose 3.9¢ in one day. Because it is a 5-day average, that jump implies current trades in roughly the mid-40s to 50s, which should keep lifting the average. Pre-Thanksgiving buying also usually firms prices in the first half of November.

(e) Over two weeks this line has moved by 6-15¢ recently. Single-week moves of 14-37¢ have happened several times in 2026. A ±15-20¢ two-week swing is plausible.

(f) No market or expert forecast covers this exact line. Seasonal norms and the firming undertone point upward. Heavy supply (inventory 15% above the 5-year median, layer flock up 5%) caps the move.

(g) Scenarios:
- Low: holiday buying finishes early and inventories keep building. Sellers discount loose eggs, and the price slides back to about 25-30¢, as it did in mid-October.
- High: a cluster of large HPAI detections in the Midwest, plus strong pre-Thanksgiving feature demand, triggers a short squeeze. The price spikes to 70-90¢, similar to the 37¢ weekly jump in early March.

- **Low:** Holiday buying finishes early and inventories keep swelling (Midwest Large already up 19%). Sellers discount loose eggs and the price falls back to the high 20s or low 20s, as in mid-October and June.
- **High:** Several large layer flocks are hit by HPAI in early November, on top of the Illinois and California losses, and coincide with peak holiday demand. Buyers scramble and the loose price jumps 30 to 50¢, as in the early March 2026 spike.
